what: a satyr warrior of Greek myth, an exile cast out of his band: a hard, scarred, scowling man above the waist and a goat below, standing on two goat legs. He has a lean weather-beaten light tan face twisted in a bitter snarl, a ragged black beard, a broken nose, long pointed ears that stick out sideways, a tangle of black hair, and two heavy, thick, ridged dark grey goat horns that rise from his forehead and curve back over his skull. From the waist down he has the hind legs of a goat: shaggy grey-black hair, backward-bending hocks and two black cloven hooves, with a short goat tail. He has realistic adult proportions: a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall.

pose: Seen from the side and a little from the front, he runs to the left on his two goat legs with his body pitched forward and his head lowered so the heavy horns point ahead to butt, one hoof lifted high, the club swung up and back behind his shoulder in his right hand, his left fist punched forward.

what: a Sobek warrior: a temple soldier of the Egyptian crocodile god, a tall, broad, powerful man standing upright on two legs with the head of a Nile crocodile set on his shoulders. The head is a real crocodile's: a long, flat, heavy snout lined with rows of big white interlocking teeth, knobbly ridged scales, and two small cold yellow eyes set high. what: a gorgon warrior, the bronze guardian bull of the old bestiaries: a heavy bull on four legs that is not alive but built of bronze by dungeon smiths and set on guard, like a suit of armour in the shape of a bull with nothing inside. Every part of it is metal. Its body is covered in rows of big overlapping bronze scales, each as large as a shield, with a raised bright rim and a row of round rivets, and deep black gaps between them. Its shoulders and haunches are great smooth domed bronze plates. Its neck is a stack of broad bronze hoops; its legs are jointed bronze tubes with black gaps at the knees; its hooves are solid bronze blocks; its tail is a chain of thick bronze links ending in a bronze spike. Streaks of dull teal verdigris run down from every seam. Its head is a bull's head hammered from bronze plate, far too heavy for it, hanging low so the muzzle almost touches the ground, with two small eyes that glow dull amber-orange. In place of horns it has two long, straight, thick bronze spear blades fixed to its brow, level and side by side, pointing straight forward past its nose. From its bronze nostrils shoots one short jet of heavy pale grey stone-dust vapour, joined to the muzzle, no longer than its own head.

what: a cairn wight: the walking corpse of a forgotten Highland poor man who was buried under nothing but a heap of stones on a hillside, the poorest and most bitter of the wights, a tall, gaunt, stooped, long-limbed dead man, plainly a corpse and plainly undead. His skin is a colour no living person has: cold pale chalk-grey, the grey of cold ash, with blue-grey shadows in the hollows, the same on his face, scalp, neck, arms, hands, legs and feet. The skin is shrunk tight on the bones so that every rib, knuckle and joint shows. His face is a dead man's: hollow cheeks, deep sunken eye sockets, a thin sharp nose, ears, and dried grey lips drawn back from long teeth; in the sockets his two eyes are blank and white with no pupils, shining with a cold light. what: a will-o'-the-wisp, the foolish fire of the marshes, the full-grown kind that travellers took for a lantern: one single large floating flame of cold ghost-light, painted as real fire, soft and glowing like the flame of burning marsh gas. It is one tall full flame shaped like a candle flame, round and wide at the bottom and drawn up to three long flickering pointed tongues at the top, the middle tongue the tallest. A big round blinding white core fills the whole heart of the flame, half as wide as the flame itself; round the core is a body of very pale blue-white fire, and only at the soft outer edges and the tips of the tongues does it deepen to bright sky blue. One short curling wisp of fading blue fire trails from the bottom of the flame, joined to it. It is only fire, soft-edged and very bright: a cold, lonely marsh light, larger, fuller and brighter than a lesser wisp.

She has a hard weather-beaten light tan face, deeply lined, with a hooked nose, a thin cruel mouth, and pale grey staring eyes ringed with soot. Her hair is a great wild mane of iron-grey, hanging to her waist in thick matted braids, and tied into it are big white bones, plain to see: six long white rib bones, each as long as her forearm, stand out from her hair round her head in a ragged fan, and two small white bird skulls hang in the braids beside her cheeks. a wild mane of dark iron-grey hair with long white bones standing out of it, readable in the small sprite
a long black dress and a black crow-feather mantle, fully clothed
a ball of violet flame in the open right palm
black withered fingers on the raised left hand
no staff and no hat

what: a wolf pack leader: a real grey wolf on four legs, the old parent of the pack, an ordinary wild timber wolf of normal size, lean, long-legged and rangy with a narrow chest, a long muzzle, upright ears and a full bushy tail. Its thick winter coat is silver-grey with a charcoal saddle along the back and a cream-white throat, chest and belly, and its muzzle has gone pale with age. It is howling.
colours: silver-grey fur on the flanks, legs and face, a charcoal-black saddle along the back and tail tip, a cream-white throat, chest and belly, a pale muzzle, amber eyes, a black nose. No tan, no orange and no brown fur anywhere.
wears: It is an animal and wears nothing.
holds: It is an animal on four legs and holds nothing.
pose: Seen from the side, facing left, on four legs: it stands with all four paws down and its front legs braced straight, its neck stretched up and its head thrown far back so the muzzle points straight up at the sky, its mouth open in a long howl, ears laid back, tail held out level behind.
must_show: a real wolf on four legs, seen from the side
head thrown back, muzzle pointing straight up, howling
silver-grey coat with a dark saddle and a cream throat, no brown
lean and ordinary-sized: lighter than the dire wolf alpha, no scars, not snarling

what: a winter wolf of the Norse frost giants: a real wolf on four legs but as tall as a horse, long-legged and deep-chested, with a long heavy muzzle, a great thick shaggy neck ruff and a heavy bushy tail. Its whole coat is pure snow-white, long and shaggy, with pale icy shadows, and it is cold to the bone: hard white frost crusts its back and shoulders, and a fringe of thick clear icicles hangs from its neck ruff, its belly fur and its tail. Its eyes are pale, bright and clever. Its jaws are open, and out of its mouth shoots one short thick jet of freezing breath, pale icy blue with white ice crystals in it, joined to the mouth and no longer than its own head.
colours: pure snow-white shaggy fur with pale icy blue shadows, the blue of a winter sky, in every part, white frost, clear pale icicles, pale ice-blue eyes, a black nose and black lips, white fangs, one short jet of pale icy blue and white breath.
wears: It is an animal and wears nothing.
holds: It is an animal on four legs and holds nothing.
pose: Seen from the side, facing left, on four legs: it stands braced with all four paws down and its legs spread, its head lowered and thrust forward at the left, jaws wide open, blowing the short jet of freezing breath straight out ahead of it, its hackles up and its icicle-hung tail held out stiff behind.
must_show: a real wolf on four legs, seen from the side, pure white all over
icicles hanging from the ruff, belly and tail, and frost on the back
one short jet of pale icy breath from the open jaws
pale ice-blue eyes
plainly not an ordinary grey wolf
must_not_show: howling with the head thrown back
long breath across the whole picture
cloud of mist round the body
spikes of ice all over like a hedgehog

what: Fenrir, the Wolf of Ragnarok, son of Loki, the wolf the gods could not hold: a monstrous wolf on four legs, the full-grown terror his collared pup will become, immensely heavy and deep-chested with a huge broad head, a bristling ridge of long black fur standing along his whole spine, a great shaggy black mane, and paws as broad as shields. His coat is black and charcoal-grey with an ash-grey muzzle and chest, and the tips of his mane and spine ridge are white with frost. His jaws are stretched impossibly wide open, wider than his own head is long, crowded with enormous white fangs as long as daggers, and his eyes burn pale icy blue with no pupils. He has broken every bond: a broad pale steel collar round his neck is snapped, with a short length of broken heavy chain, three big links, hanging against his chest; a thick iron shackle with one broken link is on each front ankle; and wound round his neck and one foreleg, torn through, streams the ribbon Gleipnir, a broad smooth ribbon of shining pale gold with its two torn ends flying behind him.
colours: black and charcoal-grey shaggy fur with an ash-grey muzzle and chest, no tan and no brown, white frost on the mane and spine ridge, burning pale icy blue eyes, the blue of a winter sky, enormous white fangs, a black mouth, a broken pale steel-grey collar and dark iron shackles, a torn ribbon of shining pale gold.
wears: He wears only his broken bonds: the snapped steel collar with its short chain, an iron shackle on each front ankle, and the torn gold ribbon.
holds: He is an animal on four legs and holds nothing.
pose: Seen from the side, facing left, on four legs: he lunges forward with his hind legs driving and his huge front paws striking down, his body horizontal, his head thrust out at the left with the enormous jaws gaping to swallow, the broken chain swinging at his chest and the torn gold ribbon streaming back along his flank.
must_show: a monstrous black and charcoal wolf on four legs, seen from the side
jaws stretched enormously wide with huge white fangs
burning pale icy eyes
a broken steel collar with a short chain, and broken shackles on the front legs
a torn shining gold ribbon streaming from the neck, readable in the small sprite
a frosted mane and spine ridge
plainly a boss: the grandest and most fearsome wolf, far beyond the pack leader and the winter wolf
must_not_show: whole unbroken chain to the ground

what: a desert wraith: the ghost of a traveller who died without tomb or rites in the Red Land of Egypt and was dried to a husk by sun and wind. It is an empty hooded shroud of sun-bleached, wind-shredded linen with nothing inside it: the hood is a deep black hollow in which burn two small fierce ember-orange lights, its eyes. Out of its long ragged sleeves reach two long, thin, dried-up husk hands, dark leather-brown like old dates, with long bony fingers. The linen is torn into long strips that whip sideways in a hot wind. Below the waist it has nothing: the shroud narrows and twists into one tight, thin, tapering spiral of blown dull red-ochre sand, a little whirlwind, joined to the cloth and ending in a point.
colours: sun-bleached undyed pale sand-beige linen with darker dun-brown folds and frayed dark edges, a black hollow hood, two ember-orange eye lights, dark leather-brown dried hands, a tapering twist of dull red-ochre sand.
wears: It is nothing but an empty tattered hooded linen shroud.
holds: Its two dried hands are empty and it holds nothing.
pose: It sweeps down and to the left through empty air on the hot wind, leaning far forward, both long husk hands reaching out ahead with the fingers spread to draw the water out of the living, its torn linen strips streaming back to the right and its twist of sand curling away behind and below.
must_show: an empty hood with two ember-orange eye lights
pale sun-bleached sand-beige linen tatters: the pale desert kin of the black wraith
two dark dried husk hands reaching, empty
the lower half narrowing to one tight twist of red-ochre sand
painted with weight and wind, not a bedsheet ghost
must_not_show: whole mummy wrapped in neat bandages
big cloud of sand round the body

what: an entropy wraith: what is left when a wraith wears through, a hole in the shape of a ghost. It is one tall hooded burial shroud of ancient cloth, worn colourless, bone-white and pale ash-grey, threadbare and brittle, hanging in the air, and it is wrapped round nothing. The hood gapes wide open at the front and the shroud hangs open down the chest, and inside there is no face and no body: only one tall, deep, pitch-black emptiness, the shape of a keyhole, large and plain, with the pale cloth folding away into it like the lip of a well. There are no eyes and no lights in the black. The pale edge of the cloth round the hollow catches a thin cold bone-white light. Two long empty sleeves reach forward, and from each hangs a long thin hand of the same pale brittle ash, the fingers crumbling away at the tips into flakes. The whole shroud is coming apart: its hem and its trailing edge break up into big square flakes and crumbs of pale ash that fall away downward, still touching it, and rust-brown stains spread up from the crumbling edges.
colours: bone-white and pale ash-grey ancient cloth with mid-grey folds, a plain neutral grey, never tinted; one large pitch-black hollow inside the hood and chest; a thin cold bone-white lit edge round the hollow; rust-brown stains at the crumbling hem; pale ash flakes.
wears: It is nothing but an empty, worn-out, colourless hooded shroud.
holds: Its two crumbling ash hands are empty and it holds nothing.
pose: It drifts slowly to the left through empty air, leaning forward, the black hollow of its hood turned to the viewer, both long sleeves stretched out ahead with the crumbling fingers spread, its hem and its trailing right edge breaking into flakes of ash that fall away behind and below it.
must_show: a pale bone-white and ash-grey hooded shroud: pale where the common wraith is black
one large pitch-black hollow where the face and chest should be, readable in the small sprite
no eyes and no lights in the hood
long pale hands crumbling at the fingertips
the hem breaking into falling flakes, rust-brown stains
painted ancient cloth with depth and folds, not a flat shape
must_not_show: cloud of dust round the body

what: a wyrm, the oldest and heaviest kind of dragon, the hoard-guarder of Beowulf: an enormous, ancient, wingless serpent-dragon, far too vast to fly. Its body is a serpent's: immensely long, thick as a great tree trunk, four times as long as it is tall, lying low with its belly on the ground, its length thrown into one slow S-curve from the head at the left to a long thick tail curling up at the right. Four short, thick, bowed legs with black claws, far too small for such a length, sprawl out from its sides like a huge lizard's. It has a long, heavy, blunt, scarred head on a long thick neck, with a jutting lower jaw full of worn yellow fangs, a short beard of horny spikes under the chin, two thick black horns sweeping straight back, and small deep-set burning orange eyes under heavy brow ridges. A row of blunt, worn, broken black spines runs down its whole back. Its scales are huge, thick, dull and battered like old shields: very dark brown, the colour of an old iron nail, nearly black in the shadows, with dull grey scars and chipped edges. The broad plates of its belly and throat are pale bone-grey, worn smooth and scratched. Soot blackens its jaws. Out of its open mouth shoots one short thick jet of orange and yellow fire, joined to the mouth, no longer than its own head.
colours: very dark brown scales the colour of an old iron nail, nearly black in the shadows, with dull grey scars, pale bone-grey belly and throat plates, black horns, claws and spines, sooty black jaws, yellow fangs, burning orange eyes, orange and yellow fire. The body is never orange and never tan.
wears: It is a beast and wears nothing.
holds: It is a beast on four legs and holds nothing.
pose: Seen from the side, facing left: it crawls forward with all four of its short legs planted on the ground and its long body horizontal and low, belly dragging, its heavy head raised a little at the left with the jaws wide open, the short jet of fire shooting straight out ahead of its mouth, its long tail curling up behind at the right.
must_show: a very long, heavy, low-slung wingless dragon crawling on four short legs, seen from the side
no wings at all
huge battered very dark brown scales and a pale worn belly, a body far longer than it is tall
black horns swept back and a row of worn spines
one short jet of fire from the jaws
old, vast and scarred, not a sleek young dragon
must_not_show: long fire across the whole picture

what: a void crawler: a thing that came through where magic wore the world thin, painted with weight, wetness and depth like a creature of the deep sea, dreadful and never cute. It is one great knot of thick tentacles and nothing else: a dozen heavy, tapering tentacles of slick hide, each as thick as a man's leg at its root, all growing out of one low central mound no bigger than a barrel. The hide is glossy as wet tar: black in its depths and dark plum-violet where the light falls on its swollen ridges, with a hard thin rim of cold bright violet light along every upper edge, and a row of pale violet rings runs down the underside of each tentacle. It has no eyes. In the middle of the central mound, facing the viewer, gapes one very wide jagged gash, as wide as the mound, crowded with two rows of long, thick, crooked bone-white fangs, each as long as a hand, plain and bright against the dark, with pitch-black emptiness behind them. The tentacles go every way: three rear straight up and curl over at the tips, three stretch far out to the left, three sprawl out to the right, and the rest coil low along its lower edge. It is never entirely present: the last part of each raised tentacle breaks up into a few torn, fading shreds of pale violet light, still joined to it.
colours: glossy black and dark plum-violet wet hide with wet pale highlights, a thin bright cold violet rim of light on its edges, pale violet rings under the limbs, large bone-white fangs, a pitch-black mouth, a few fading shreds of pale violet light at the limb tips.
wears: It wears nothing.
holds: It holds nothing.
pose: The knot of tentacles rolls and drags itself to the left, lopsided, the three left tentacles stretched out long to seize, three reared high and curling, the fanged gash in the central mound gaping wide, the raised tips fraying into shreds of pale light. It is one joined mass with a clean lower edge and nothing under it.
must_show: a knot of many thick tentacles round a small central mound, glossy dark hide with violet highlights: painted with depth and wet shine, not a flat black shape, and not a four-legged beast
a thin bright violet lit edge that makes it readable on a dark floor
one very wide gash of big bone-white fangs, readable in the small sprite
thick tapering tentacles reaching up, left and right
tentacle tips fraying into shreds of pale violet light
no eyes

what: a void leviathan: the sea beast of the Book of Job grown vaster and swimming not in any sea but in the dark between worlds, painted with weight and depth like a monster of the deepest ocean, dreadful and never cute. It is one immense, thick, heavy, armoured serpent, a giant eel-like body as thick as a tower, thrown into two great rolling loops. Its back is covered in huge overlapping ridged plates, deep indigo-black, each plate edged with a thin line of cold pale cyan light, and along each flank runs a row of large round spots that glow pale cyan like the lights of a deep-sea fish. Its underside is banded with paler slate-grey plates. A tall ragged spiny fin runs down its spine. Its head, at the left, is enormous, blunt and armoured, with a huge underslung lower jaw; the jaws gape wide, lined with very long, curved, needle-sharp bone-white fangs, plain and bright, and the inside of the mouth is pitch-black emptiness. Two small cold eyes glow pale cyan, narrow slanted slits with no pupils, set far back on the head. Parts of its length are always elsewhere: in the middle of one loop the body simply stops in a ragged edge of pale cyan light, there is a short gap of empty air, and then the body goes on again from a second ragged lit edge. Its tail tapers to a point.
colours: deep indigo-black and dark slate armoured plates, each edged with thin cold pale cyan light, paler slate-grey belly bands, a row of glowing pale cyan spots along the flank, narrow pale cyan eye slits, long bone-white fangs, a pitch-black mouth.
wears: It wears nothing.
holds: It holds nothing.
pose: Seen from the side, it surges to the left through empty air, its huge head thrust forward and low at the left with the fanged jaws gaping to swallow, its body rolling up behind in two heavy loops that begin to close like a crushing coil, its spiny fin raised, its tail whipping up at the right. Nothing is under it.
must_show: one immense armoured serpent in heavy loops, painted with depth, not a flat black shape
deep indigo-black plates with thin pale cyan lit edges, readable on a dark floor
a row of glowing pale cyan spots along the flank
a huge gaping jaw of long bone-white fangs, readable in the small sprite
plainly grander and more solid than the void crawler: armoured, finned and vast

what: a void wyrm: a dragon that flew too far into the dark between the stars and came back with some of it. It is a great lean dragon that walks on all four legs like a huge lizard, with a long neck, a long whip tail and two great bat-like wings. Its scales show no colour: it is covered in large plates and scales as big as a hand, each one dead matt black in the middle with a broad, bright, hard edge of cold silver-white starlight, so the whole dragon gleams like black armour trimmed with polished silver. A bright silver-white ridge of spines runs down its neck, back and tail, its throat and belly are banded with pale silver-grey plates, and its claws are silver-white. Its head is long, narrow and cruel, with a crown of four long straight horns of bright silver-white, and two blank eyes that glow solid silver-white with no pupils. The membranes of its wings are deep midnight darkness, and each wing holds five very large, bright white four-pointed stars, each as big as the dragon's eye socket is wide many times over, as big as its paw, like windows on the night sky; the wing bones are bright silver-white. Out of its open jaws shoots one short jet of tearing wrongness: a thick ragged tongue of blinding silver-white light with a black core, joined to the mouth, no longer than its own head.
colours: dead matt black scales, each with a broad bright cold silver-white edge, a bright silver-white spine ridge, horns, claws and wing bones, pale silver-grey throat and belly plates, deep midnight-dark wing membranes with very large bright white stars, solid silver-white glowing eyes, one short jet of silver-white light with a black core. No violet, no red.
wears: It is a beast and wears nothing.
holds: It is a beast on four legs and holds nothing.
pose: Seen from the side, facing left: all four of its feet are planted on the ground and its body is horizontal, its long neck stretched forward and low at the left with the jaws wide open spitting the short jet of silver-white light, both wings raised high above its back and spread, showing their starry membranes, its long tail whipping out behind at the right.
must_show: a dragon on four legs with its body horizontal, seen from the side
black scales each rimmed with bright silver-white light: readable on a dark floor, not a flat black shape
raised wings whose dark membranes hold large white stars
solid silver-white glowing eyes and silver-edged black horns
a short jet of silver-white light from the jaws
plainly a dragon of the void: no colour in it but black and silver
must_not_show: long breath across the whole picture

what: a void seraph: one of the six-winged seraphim that Isaiah saw above the throne, fallen, and emptied. It is a very tall, slender, solemn hooded figure hanging upright in the air, with six great wings of black feathers. Four of the wings are spread behind it, in two separate pairs, one pair above the other. The upper pair is large and lifted high, slanting up and outward above its shoulders. The lower pair is a second, separate pair of smaller wings that grows from the small of its back: these two droop down and outward, their tips pointing at the lower corners of the picture, well below its elbows. On each side a wide wedge of empty backdrop shows between the upper wing and the lower wing. The last two wings are folded shut round its lower body: from the waist down it is wrapped in black feathers, a long closed sheath of two folded wings that narrows to a point at the bottom, in place of any skirt. Every feather is glossy black with a thin edge of pale tarnished-gold light, and the wings are painted feather by feather with depth. From the waist up it wears a pale ash-white robe with long sleeves and a deep hood. Inside the hood there is no face: only one smooth oval of pitch-black emptiness, large and plain, ringed by a thin band of pale gold light where the hood's edge catches it. Above the hood floats a thin halo of dull tarnished gold with a wide gap broken out of it, close to the head. Its two long thin hands are ash-grey.
colours: six wings of glossy black feathers, each feather edged with pale tarnished-gold light; a long pale ash-white hooded robe with grey folds and a frayed hem; one pitch-black oval hollow inside the hood, ringed with thin pale gold light; a thin broken halo of dull tarnished gold; long ash-grey hands; a long black lance with a thin pale gold lit edge.
wears: From the waist up it wears a plain pale ash-white robe with long sleeves and a deep hood, tied at the waist with a plain cord of dull gold. Below the cord there is no cloth, only the two folded black wings wrapped round it down to a point. No armour, no crown.
holds: It holds exactly one lance in its right hand, gripped at the middle and held slanting across the front of its pale robe with the point aimed down to the left: one long, straight shaft of pure black as thick as its wrist, ending in a broad black leaf-shaped spear blade as long as its forearm, with a line of pale gold light along the blade's edges. Its left hand is empty, a long ash-grey hand raised open beside the hood, palm out. It holds nothing else.
pose: It hangs upright in empty air, leaning forward and to the left, the large upper pair of wings lifted high, the smaller lower pair drooping down and outward beneath them, and two more wrapped shut round its lower body, the black hollow of the hood turned to the viewer, its right arm driving the black lance down and to the left across its body, its left hand raised palm out.
must_show: a tall hooded figure with four black wings spread in an X behind it and two more folded round its lower body in a sheath of black feathers, six in all
feathers edged with pale gold light: readable on a dark floor
a hood with no face in it, only a pitch-black oval ringed with pale gold light, readable in the small sprite
a thin broken gold halo
exactly one long black lance with a broad spear blade in the right hand, readable in the small sprite
an empty raised left hand
solemn, fallen and terrible: the grandest of the void creatures
must_not_show: long white robe to the ground
big halo of light round the body
